signals.question: How are merchants receiving payments in Yaba?
signals.title: Reported primary payment methods
signals.answer: Of 114 classifiable responses, 70 named transfers, 39 cash and 5 POS/card as the method receiving the largest share of customer payments.
signals.context: 114 classifiable responses from 115 eligible initial observations. 0 missing, 1 unknown or unrecognised, 0 contradictory, 0 not applicable. Only classifiable responses enter this signal’s denominator.
signals.limitations: Non-representative field cohort; self-reported responses. 27 included observations have unresolved identity-review flags and may include repeat submissions. Observations are not verified unique businesses. No national estimates or causal claims. These are reported primary methods, not transaction volumes or market shares.

signals.question: Do merchants keep track of their sales records?
signals.title: Reported recordkeeping practices
signals.answer: 56 of 112 classifiable responses selected “No records”. 56 selected another recognised response. Mixed “No records” selections and unrecognised options are held out.
signals.context: 112 classifiable responses from 115 eligible initial observations. 0 missing, 2 unknown or unrecognised, 1 contradictory, 0 not applicable. Only classifiable responses enter this signal’s denominator.
signals.limitations: Non-representative field cohort; self-reported responses. 27 included observations have unresolved identity-review flags and may include repeat submissions. Observations are not verified unique businesses. No national estimates or causal claims. The combined “Memory Notebook/paper” option cannot distinguish memory from written records. Payment and recordkeeping totals do not establish individual overlap.

signals.question: Are trading conditions improving?
signals.title: Recalled business conditions over three months
signals.answer: Of 114 classifiable responses, 89 described business as better than about three months earlier, 16 about the same and 9 worse.
signals.context: 114 classifiable responses from 115 eligible initial observations. 0 missing, 1 unknown or unrecognised, 0 contradictory, 0 not applicable. Only classifiable responses enter this signal’s denominator.
signals.limitations: Non-representative field cohort; self-reported responses. 27 included observations have unresolved identity-review flags and may include repeat submissions. Observations are not verified unique businesses. No national estimates or causal claims. Retrospective recollection at an initial visit is not measured longitudinal change. “Too new to say” is excluded.

signals.question: Are restocking costs changing?
signals.title: Reported restocking expenditure
signals.answer: Among 104 classifiable responses from businesses that restock, 85 reported higher expenditure, 18 about the same and 1 lower than about three months earlier.
signals.context: 104 classifiable responses from 115 eligible initial observations. 0 missing, 1 unknown or unrecognised, 0 contradictory, 10 not applicable. Only classifiable responses enter this signal’s denominator.
signals.limitations: Non-representative field cohort; self-reported responses. 27 included observations have unresolved identity-review flags and may include repeat submissions. Observations are not verified unique businesses. No national estimates or causal claims. Expenditure can change with prices, quantities or product mix. This does not measure price inflation or profit margins.

signals.question: Where does ERI have evidence today?
signals.title: Current published cohort
signals.answer: 115 eligible initial observations dated 7 October 2026 – 16 October 2026 are included in this analysis of the configured Yaba–Sabo–Tejuosho cohort in Lagos. 27 identity-review observations are included with warnings, and 1 shifted source rows were recovered. 0 source rows are held out of the published cohort.
signals.context: Geography is the configured scope of this source; the form has no row-level market field. The historical 10-record pilot is not added to this source. No verified longitudinal comparison is published.
